title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 41-43). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'classification' (also called 'schéma'): a set A of figures with several relations. These are an order-type relation ⊴, an incompatibility or disjointness relation |·|, and a primitive relation ≪ with a strengthened form ˚≪. From (A, ⊴, |·|) he builds an ordered set Σ of 'supports', with a bottom element ∅_Σ and an intersection. To each figure X he attaches a set Dép(X) ⊂ Σ of 'déploiements' (deployments). Distinct deployments T ≠ T' of the same figure are disjoint (T |·| T', hence T∩T' = ∅). He also uses distinguished maximal chains X° in X̃ (equivalently in Dép X).

Previous page. If X ≪ Y there is a canonical increasing map φ: X̃ → Ỹ. In terms of deployments this is an increasing map ψ: Dép X → Dép Y with S ≤ ψ(S) for every S.

This page.
(1) ψ is unique. Suppose S ≠ ∅_Σ satisfies S ≤ T and S ≤ T' with T, T' ∈ Dép Y and T ≠ T'. Then T∩T' = ∅, so S ≤ ∅, so S = ∅. Hence each nonempty S has at most one deployment of Y above it.
(2) This gives a necessary condition for X ≪ Y, stated purely in terms of deployments. Condition R: for every S ∈ Dép X there exists a T ∈ Dép Y, necessarily unique and written T = ψ(S), with S ≤ T. Moreover the resulting map ψ: Dép X → Dép Y is increasing.
(3) For the strengthened relation: X ˚≪ Y if moreover ψ sends the maximal chains X° to the maximal chains Y°, i.e. X° ≤ Y°. The NB says this presupposes X ≪ Y is already known.
(4) Margin note, only partly legible. It concerns the case X ⊴ Y, where there are maps ψ: Dép X → Dép Y and, it seems, Dép(X) ⊂ Dép(Y).
(5) Definition. A classification is 'spatial' if the necessary condition R on Dép X and Dép Y is also sufficient for X ≪ Y.

Next page, motivation. In a spatial classification the primitive relation ≪ is recoverable from purely spatial data (⊴, |·|, supports as 'occupied space'). This raises a realizability question: when does a structure (A, ⊴, |·|) come from a spatial schema (A, ⊴, ˚≪, |·|)?

Purpose. Grothendieck is trying to reduce an abstract 'refinement/subordination' relation between figures to a purely mereological-spatial one, and to characterize which abstract structures arise this way.
errors: No mathematical error. Uniqueness relies on distinct deployments of Y being disjoint, which is an axiom fixed earlier. It also needs S ≠ ∅_Σ, a proviso stated on the previous page.

'De plus, l'application est croissante' is asserted rather than proved here. Under R alone, monotonicity is an extra requirement unless the order on Dép forces it. Grothendieck seems to include it in the condition.
Minor notational drift: the map is called φ in the transcription but ψ on the previous page and probably in the handwriting (T = ψ(S)).

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the deployment of Y dominating a nonempty deployment of X, because distinct deployments are pairwise disjoint
ideas.modern_name: refinement map between partitions / covers by disjoint pieces (coarsening map)

ideas.what: Necessary condition R for X ≪ Y: every deployment of X lies in some deployment of Y, with the induced map increasing; ˚≪ adds that maximal chains go to maximal chains
ideas.modern_name: refinement / subordination of decompositions, expressed via a support map

ideas.what: Definition of a 'spatial' classification: the primitive relation ≪ is fully determined by the support-theoretic condition R
ideas.modern_name: analogous to 'spatial' locales or sober representability: an abstract structure determined by its spatial or point-set realization; also close to mereotopology (part-of plus disjointness)
ideas.usually_credited_to: spatial locales: Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone; mereotopology: Whitehead, Leśniewski, Clarke

ideas.what: Realizability question (next page): when does (A, ⊴, |·|) come from a spatial schema?
ideas.usually_credited_to: mereotopology representation theorems (e.g. Stone-type representations of contact algebras, Düntsch–Winter)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of figures, supports, disjointness |·| and the notion of a 'spatial' classification is an independent version of point-free mereotopology. The question of when an abstract relation reduces to 'occupied space' parallels representation theorems for contact algebras and spatiality of locales. No link to that literature seems to have been drawn.
missed.quote: On dit qu'une classification est spatiale, si la condition nécessaire précédente R, sur Dép X et Dép Y, pour que l'on ait X≪Y [est] aussi suffisante.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working on point-free 'spatial' foundations in 1986. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an elementary uniqueness argument and a definition. It is historically interesting as part of an unpublished axiomatics of figures and 'spatial' classifications, but carries no deep result.
transcription_corrections: 'on termes des' should read 'en termes des'.
The map is most likely written ψ, not φ, consistent with the previous page: '(nécessairement unique, noté T=ψ(S))', 'ψ : Dép(X)→Dép(Y)'.
'De plus, on a X ˚≪ Y dès l'application' should read 'dès que l'application ψ précédente transforme les plus grandes chaînes X° en les plus grandes chaînes Y°'.
'si est [...] condition si on a' is likely 'i.e. si et seulement si on a'.
'R∀' is the label 'R' with a struck-out '∀'.
Margin begins approximately 'Si l'on a X ⊴ Y, ψ : Dép X → Dép Y ... Dép(X) ⊂ Dép(Y) ...'. This is a remark on the case X ⊴ Y, not '△_{Y,Y}'.
The final line ends 'pour que l'on ait X≪Y' and continues on the next page with 'est aussi suffisante'.
